what_happened: Direct live evidence for this task's Part B, stronger than originally reported. Invoked 'orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh --session <sid> --state-file specs/state.json 373' passing ONLY task 373. The PLAN CACHE REPLAY returned the cached composition verbatim, which contained a blocked[] row for task 372 reading 'task #372 is partial with 1 unresolved blocker(s) and no continuation; needs human' -- even though (a) 372 was NOT in the argument list, and (b) 372's status at that moment was already 'completed'. So the replay ignores BOTH the --force-phases argument (the originally reported symptom, decision D3) AND the task-number argument list, and serves a verdict contradicting current state.json. Mechanism corroborated: the cache was written by the cycle whose only output was an aux_dispatch[] row (blocker-research for 372), and skill-orchestrate's own Move 2 MUST NOT states 'an aux_dispatch[] row never reaches Move 3' -- so cycle-postflight (the single site that clears plan_cache, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh:1854) can never run for an aux-only cycle, leaving the entry replayable indefinitely. This answers this task's own first research step without further investigation. Consequence observed: the batch could not be advanced through the engine at all; both remaining tasks had to be completed via out-of-band direct dispatch instead.

Found that plan-file-scope-harvest.sh already unions each plan phase's Files-to-modify field into file_scope at plan-postflight time, and that orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's existing file_scope_collision directory-prefix overlap already covers a declared wide source-store sentinel -- Part A's whole-tree-claim design needs zero new admission-gate code, only a plan-authoring convention. Also confirmed Part B's mechanical lead (aux_dispatch mints dispatch_seq_counter but never reaches orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, the sole plan_cache clear site) directly via SKILL.md line 185 and the mint/clear call sites.

Planning verification contradicted a load-bearing research-report claim: the report asserted that reusing file_scope_collision for the whole-tree claim 'automatically inherits that branch's EXISTING --phase-map exemption with no new code'. Code read of orchestrate-batch-admit.sh shows the collision branch never reads $phase_group -- only the self_modifying branch (line 789) and the absent_file_scope branch (line 845) do. Two further disqualifiers also surfaced: validate-state.sh Check 8 flags exactly the trailing-slash whole-directory-root entry the report recommended adopting as a convention, and a real wide path entry would loosen path_covered_by_scope()'s containment guard consumed by git-snapshot.sh. Plan therefore chose a reserved slashless sentinel plus a new last-ranked admission dimension instead of the report's zero-code recommendation.

plan-file-scope-harvest.sh is already path-shape-agnostic (its own header: 'the first backtick-delimited token on that line is the path', and it 'never stats, resolves, or filesystem-validates a harvested path'), so the chosen reserved-sentinel declaration needs ZERO parser change -- only a test case pinning that it stays so. Equally, the existing __FULL_SWEEP__ and __MISSING__ tokens gave a settled in-repo convention for the sentinel's spelling, and file_scope_collision's already-narrowed v5 deferral-direction rule supplied a proven in_batch/cross_batch rule the new dimension reuses verbatim instead of inventing one. Three design sub-decisions resolved by existing machinery rather than new code.

Phase 2's WHOLE-TREE-CODISPATCH fixture (two in-batch candidates with disjoint real file_scope, each also declaring the __WHOLE_TREE__ sentinel) revealed that TODAY's unmodified orchestrate-batch-admit.sh already defers the higher-numbered candidate -- but via the EXISTING file_scope_collision exact-match branch (both candidates declare the identical literal '__WHOLE_TREE__' string, which is a trivial exact match under scopes_overlap_first), not via an 'admit' false negative as the plan's Design Decisions section assumed. The plan's stated Part A mechanism ('a new, fifth admission dimension... evaluated LAST... only on a candidate the three existing post-absence branches would otherwise ADMIT... no existing branch's code path is edited') cannot work as literally specified for the same-sentinel in-batch case: the existing exact-match collision scan intercepts and defers with defer_reason=file_scope_collision (wrong reason, no claim_sentinel/whole_tree_claim fields) BEFORE the new last-ranked dimension would ever be reached. Phase 4 must resolve this tension -- either let the new dimension run before (or short-circuit) the plain file_scope_collision scan specifically when the colliding entry equals the reserved sentinel, or relabel/augment that specific collision case in place. The red-baseline fixture itself is unaffected (today's output is still provably wrong against the target defer_reason/fields, so RED holds), but Phase 4's claimed zero-existing-branch-edit approach needs a design update.

Phase 4's Scope Hypothesis grep (orchestrate-batch-admit-v6 literal enumeration) found two consumers beyond the plan's declared Files-to-modify list for this phase: scripts/orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh (a prose comment naming the schema version, not a strict assertion) and scripts/test-conflict-predicate.sh (a strict literal $schema pin in its own Group 3 non-regression case, which would have started failing once the v6->v7 bump landed). Both were updated to v7 alongside the planned files, since the change is mechanical, low-risk, and required to avoid breaking test-conflict-predicate.sh's own suite; docs/architecture/batch-admit-schema.md was deliberately left at v6 for now since its Version History entry is Phase 6's own explicitly-assigned task, not Phase 4's.

Resolved Phase 2's recorded design-gap finding (the exact-match collision scan intercepts a same-sentinel in-batch pair before a naively-appended-last new dimension would ever run) by RELABELING the existing $hit collision in place rather than adding a separate scan: when $hit.ov_path equals the reserved whole_tree_claim_sentinel, the verdict is built with defer_reason whole_tree_claim (plus claim_sentinel/colliding_task_number/colliding_task_status/collision_scope and the research/plan --phase-map exemption) instead of falling through to plain file_scope_collision; any real-path collision is completely untouched. This reuses the collision scan's own admitted-set-only in_batch / in_flight-cross_batch deferral-direction selection verbatim, satisfying the plan's Design Decision without editing that selection logic at all. Both previously-red Phase 2 fixtures (WHOLE-TREE-CODISPATCH, WHOLE-TREE-PHASE-EXEMPT) now pass, with zero regression across the other 13 pre-existing cases in that suite plus the 382 cases in test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh.
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/orchestrate-suggest-next-batch.sh' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/test-conflict-predicate.sh' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.

Phase 6's Scope Hypothesis grep (absent_file_scope|file_scope_collision across context/ and docs/) led to inspecting docs/architecture/batch-admit-schema.md's Version History, which documents that EVERY prior defer_reason bump (v2 self_modifying, v4 session_active, v6 absent_file_scope) added a matching case arm to orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's closed 'case $dr in ... esac' block in the SAME change that introduced the new defer_reason -- Phase 4 (orchestrate-batch-admit.sh only, per its own declared Files-to-modify list) did not add a whole_tree_claim arm there. Without it, every whole_tree_claim defer would have silently fallen into the loud default/unrecognized arm: excluded from dispatch (correct practical effect) but recorded into unrecognized_defer_reason_ledger with a scary 'UNRECOGNIZED defer_reason' WARNING, rather than a clean defer_ledger entry -- exactly the gap class that default arm's own comment warns against ('If this is a new defer_reason value, add a matching case arm here'). Fixed now: a new whole_tree_claim) case arm added to orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh mirroring file_scope_collision's shape (collision_scope preserved, no --allow-X bypass), plus a new Group 34b regression case in test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh confirming the defer_ledger entry (not unrecognized) and the absence of the loud warning. All tests green, no regression.
